questions.q:
Which of the following interchange of numbers and signs would make the given equation correct?

512 × 64 ÷ 5 + 30 - 50 = 20
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

Option 1) : 50 and 64, + and ×

Given equation is : 512 × 64 ÷ 5 + 30 - 50 = 20

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 512 + 50 ÷ 5 × 30 - 64 = 20

⇒ 512 + 50 ÷ 5 × 30 - 64 = 20

⇒ 512 + 10 × 30 - 64 = 20

⇒ 512 + 300 - 64 = 20

⇒ 812 - 64 = 20

⇒ 748 ≠ 20

Option 2) : 20 and 30, + and ÷

Given equation is : 512 × 64 ÷ 5 + 30 - 50 = 20

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 512 × 64 + 5 ÷ 20 - 50 = 30

⇒ 512 × 64 + 5 ÷ 20 - 50 = 30

⇒ 512 × 64 + 0.25 - 50 = 30

⇒ 32768 + 0.25 - 50 = 30

⇒ 32768.25 - 50 = 30

⇒ 32718.25 ≠ 30

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : 20 and 50, × and ÷

Given equation is : 512 × 64 ÷ 5 + 30 - 50 = 20

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 512 ÷ 64 × 5 + 30 - 20 = 50

⇒ 512 ÷ 64 × 5 + 30 - 20 = 50

⇒ 8 × 5 + 30 - 20 = 50

⇒ 40 + 30 - 20 = 50

⇒ 70 - 20 = 50

⇒ 50 = 50

LHS = RHS

Option 4) : 5 and 20, + and -

Given equation is : 512 × 64 ÷ 5 + 30 - 50 = 20

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 512 × 64 ÷ 20 - 30 + 50 = 5

⇒ 512 × 64 ÷ 20 - 30 + 50 = 5

⇒ 512 × 3.2 - 30 + 50 = 5

⇒ 1638.4 - 30 + 50 = 5

⇒ 1688.4 - 30 = 5

⇒ 1658.4 ≠ 5

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "20 and 50, × and ÷ ".

questions.q: What is the percentage composition of the element of H₂SO₃?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2.5% H, 39% S, 58.5% O.

Key Points

• H2SO3

• ​It consists of two hydrogen (H) atoms, one sulfur (S) atom, and three oxygen (O) atoms.

• Pure sulfurous acid is a heavy, colorless liquid that is stable only at low temperatures. However, in practice, sulfurous acid is usually used as an aqueous solution.

• Sulfurous acid is a weak acid. It can donate two protons (H+ ions) to an aqueous solution.

• The percentage composition of the element of H2SO3 is 2.5% H, 39% S, 58.5% O.

•

H₂SO₃ => (2 x Atomic mass of hydrogen) + Atomic mass of sulfur + (3 x Atomic mass of oxygen) => (2 x 1) + 32 + (3 x 16) => 2 + 32 + 48 => 82 g/mol

Calculate the percentage composition:

Hydrogen: (2 / 82) x 100% = 2.44% approximately equals 2.5%

Sulfur: (32 / 82) x 100% = 39.02% approximately equals 39%

Oxygen: (48 / 82) x 100% = 58.53% approximately equals 58.5%

• It is produced from the reaction of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) with water (H₂O). The non-balanced chemical reaction is: SO₂ + H₂O -> H₂SO₃

• While not commonly used in its pure form due to instability, it is often used in the form of its salts, known as sulfites. Sulfites are commonly used as preservatives in food and drink to prevent discoloration and prolong shelf life.

• Sulfurous acid and its salts (sulfites) can cause allergic reactions in some people, particularly in high concentrations, causing symptoms such as breathing difficulties, skin rashes, and digestive problems. As such, usage of sulfites in food and beverages is subject to regulation in many countries.

questions.q: Which is the correct sequence of lakes according to depth (from maximum to minimum) ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Baikal > Tanganyika > Caspian Sea > Vostok.

Key Points

• Lake Baikal:

• It is located in Siberia, Russia, Lake Baikal is the largest freshwater lake by volume in the world, containing about 23% of the world's fresh surface water.

• It is also considered the deepest lake in the world, with a max depth of about 5,387 feet.

• It is known for its remarkable clarity and biodiversity, with more than 1,700 species of plants and animals, two-thirds of which can be found nowhere else in the world.

• Lake Tanganyika:

• This is the second oldest freshwater lake in the world, second largest by volume, and the second deepest, in both cases after Lake Baikal.

• It is located in East Africa, bordered by four countries - Tanzania, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Burundi, and Zambia.

• The lake is highly biodiverse, with an estimated 1,500-2,000 species, approximately 600 of which are endemic.

• Caspian Sea:

• Despite its name, the Caspian Sea is often considered the world's largest lake; it's over three times the size of the next largest lake, Lake Superior.

• It is located between Europe and Asia with five surrounding countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

•

• Lake Vostok:

• This is the largest of Antarctica's almost 400 known subglacial lakes. It is located beneath Russia's Vostok Station, under more than 4 kilometers of ice.

• The lake has been cut off from the rest of the world for somewhere between 15 and 25 million years, leading to speculation that its depths may contain unique microbial life forms that have evolved in isolation.

• Drilling projects have been undertaken to study the unexplored lake, but with significant concern to prevent contamination.

• It is a natural biopolymer found in the cell walls of fungi, the exoskeletons of arthropods (such as insects, spiders, and crustaceans), and some other invertebrate organisms.

• It is chemically composed of long chains of N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) molecules linked together.

• Chitin is closely related to another biopolymer called chitosan, which is derived from chitin through a deacetylation process.

• It's a widely used ingredient in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries due to its unique gelling, thickening, and binding properties.

• It is a natural polysaccharide extracted from various types of brown seaweed, also known as brown algae.

• It's a hydrocolloid, meaning it can absorb and hold water, forming gels and providing texture to a variety of products.

• Alginate has numerous applications in the food, pharmaceutical, and industrial sectors, thanks to its gelling, thickening, stabilizing, and film-forming properties.

questions.solution:

Key Points

• Hind Swaraj:-

• Hind Swaraj was written by Mahatma Gandhi in 1909.

• In this book, Gandhiji declared that British rule was established in India with the cooperation of Indians and had survived with their cooperation only.

• He added that if Indians had refused to cooperate, British rule would have collapsed and led to Swaraj.

• Mahatma Gandhi:-

• Mahatma Gandhi was a social reformist and leader of the Indian Independence Movement who introduced the idea of nonviolent resistance called Satyagraha.

• Birth: 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar (Gujarat)

• Brief Profile: Lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer who became the leader of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India.

• Death: He was shot dead by Nathuram Godse on 30th January 1948.

• 30th January is observed as Martyrs' Day.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji:-

• He was also known as the "Grand Old Man of India,"

• Naoroji was a Parsi intellectual, educator, cotton trader, and an early political and social leader.

• He was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.

• Naoroji served as a Member of Parliament (MP) in the United Kingdom House of Commons as a Liberal Party member.

• He is also credited with the founding of the concept of "Drain of Wealth" that held that Britain was taking away India's resources, leading to India's impoverishment.

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak:-

• He is known as Lokmanya Tilak.

• He was an Indian nationalist, teacher, and an eminent independence activist.

• He was the first leader of the Indian Independence Movement and is best known for his slogan "Swaraj (Self-rule) is my birthright and I shall have it!" adopted by the Indian independence movement.

• Tilak was one of the first and strongest advocates of "Swaraj" and a strong radical during the Indian Independence Movement.

• He is known for his attempts to mobilize Indian masses through religious symbolism, such as turning the annual domestic festival into a grand public event.

• Annie Besant:-

• She was born in Britain, Besant was a social reformer, women's rights activist, writer, orator, educationist, and prominent theosophist.

• She moved to India in 1893 and became a leader in the Indian National Congress.

• She launched the Home Rule League in 1916, aiming for dominion status for India.

• Besant was the first woman president of the Indian National Congress.

questions.q: The speed of a boat down the stream is 125% of the speed in still water. If the boat takes 30 minutes to cover 20 km in still water, then how much time (in hours) will it take to cover 15 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio Downstream : Still water = 125% : 100% = 5 : 4

Stream speed ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 part, so Upstream speed ratio = 4 − 1 = 3 parts.

Speed in still water (4 parts) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hr = 40 km/h.

Upstream speed (3 parts) = (40 ÷ 4) × 3 = 30 km/h.

Time for 15 km upstream = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour.

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Speed downstream = 125% of speed in still water.

⇒ Time taken to cover 20 km in still water = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours.

Formula Used:

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = Boat Speed (B) + Stream Speed (S)

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = Boat Speed (B) − Stream Speed (S)



Calculations:

⇒ Speed in still water (B) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hours = 40 km/h

⇒ Speed downstream (D) = 125% of 40 = 1.25 × 40 = 50 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream (S) = D − B = 50 − 40 = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed upstream (U) = B − S = 40 − 10 = 30 km/h

⇒ Time to cover 15 km upstream = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

⇒ Time = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.

Additional Information

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: B = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: S = (D − U) ÷ 2

Average Speed of Journey

If a boat goes a certain distance downstream and comes back upstream, the average speed is (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
